items.title: [First flight, 120 feet in 12 seconds, 10:35 a.m.; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina]
items.evidence: LoC catalogue record https://www.loc.gov/item/00652085/: title '[First flight, 120 feet in 12 seconds, 10:35 a.m.; Kitty Hawk, North Carolina]'; created/published '[1903 Dec. 17]'; reproduction no. 'LC-DIG-ppprs-00626 (digital file from original); LC-W861-35 (b&w film copy neg.); LC-USZ62-6166A (b&w film copy neg.)'; call no. 'LC-W86- 35 (Cabinet A) [P&P]'; medium '1 photograph : glass negative, dry plate ; plate 18 x 12.5 cm (5 x 7 format).'; notes: Title and subject note from: Wilbur & Orville Wright, pictorial materials: a documentary guide / Arthur G. Renstrom. Washington: Library of Congress, 1982, p. 57. | Attributed to Wilbur and/or Orville Wright. | Forms part of: Glass negatives from the Papers of Wilbur and Orville Wright. | Summary: 'Photograph shows the first powered, controlled, sustained flight. Orville Wright at the controls of the machine, lying prone on the lower wing with hips in the cradle which operated the wing-warping mechanism. Wilbur Wright running alongside to balance the machine, has just released his hold on the forward upright of the right wing.  The starting rail, the wing-rest, a coil box, and other items needed for flight preparation are visible behind the machine. (Orville Wright preset the camera and had John T. Daniels squeeze the rubber bulb, tripping the shutter.)' | File: https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/master/pnp/ppprs/00600/00626u.tif (master TIFF, converted to JPEG q95 at full size; source.tif kept).

items.depicts: B&w glass-negative scan, landscape. The 1903 Flyer just off the ground (about 2 ft up), centre, seen from the front-left quarter, pilot lying prone on the lower wing; a man in a dark suit and cap (Wilbur, per the catalogue) stands at right watching; the long wooden starting rail runs from lower left towards the machine; a small wooden wing-rest bench in the mid-foreground; coil box and tools on the sand at right. Flat sand and low dunes to a hazy horizon. Plate faults: white broken-off corner bottom left, a pale ghost smudge at the far left edge, two dark stains bottom centre, black plate edge at right. Tonally a bit flat/greyish.

items.title: O. & W. Wright, Flying-Machine, US Patent No. 821,393, drawing sheet 1 of 3 (Fig. 1)
items.depicts: Patent drawing sheet, vertical, black line art on white (1-bit, 300 dpi). Header: 'No. 821,393. PATENTED MAY 22, 1906. O. & W. WRIGHT. FLYING MACHINE. APPLICATION FILED MAR. 23, 1903. 3 SHEETS-SHEET 1.' Fig. 1: perspective drawing of the biplane, its wingspan running vertically down the sheet, with numbered struts and diagonal bracing wires (8, 12, 15, 19...); the forward horizontal rudder (elevator) on outriggers at right, the vertical tail rudder (22) at left; dashed lines show the wing in its warped position; 'FIG. 1.' lettered at left. Bottom: 'WITNESSES:' with two handwritten signatures, and 'INVENTORS. Orville Wright, Wilbur Wright, BY [attorney signature], ATTORNEY.' The drawing shows the glider-type wing-warping machine with no engine or propellers. It is the patented control system, not the powered 1903 Flyer.
items.evidence: Google Patents US821393A 'Flying-machine.', inventors Orville Wright and Wilbur Wright; filingDate/priorityDate 1903-03-23, publicationDate 1906-05-22 (page metadata). Sheet header read off the image (quoted in 'depicts'). Full-size drawing image from the page's itemprop='full' link; the PDF (10 pages) embeds the same 2320x3408 300 dpi CCITT scans, so the PNG is the highest resolution on offer. Delivered file is an 8-bit greyscale PNG of that 1-bit scan, verified pixel-identical (lossless), which scales without aliasing in the edit; the 1-bit original is US821393-drawings-page-1.png (= source.png) in the same folder.
items.licence: Public domain: a US patent document issued 1906 (USPTO publication, US government work, no copyright). Google Patents copy of the USPTO scan. Commercial use OK.

notes: 9 stills, all b&w, all commercially usable (LoC 'No known restrictions' Wright Brothers glass negatives + a US patent). Items 01-03 were reused from the earlier run; 04-08 were downloaded by a concurrently running duplicate agent into this same folder during this run (I verified each file against its LoC record and looked at every image); 09 (patent) was downloaded by me. LoC JPEGs are full-size 8-bit conversions of the LoC 'u' master TIFF (5000 px long side); 16-bit archival 'a' TIFFs (~245 MB each, larger) exist at the archival_tiff URL if deeper zooms are needed. Dating: only 01 is the 17 Dec 1903 first flight; 07 is 14 Dec 1903 (failed trial); 06 is 24 Nov 1903; 08 is undated 1903; 04/05 are Oct 1902 gliders. The NARA original ink patent drawing could not be fetched (archives.gov 502 x3). A duplicate agent wrote an equivalent manifest (same 9 items) at 16:27; it is kept as manifest.other_agent.json. In 09_ the files source.png and US821393-drawings-page-1.png are the same download.
